sections.overview: Saxatilomys paulinae is a poorly known murid rodent first described from limestone karst in central Laos.
sections.identification: It has dark, dense fur with partly spine-like hairs and unusually enlarged pads on its feet.
sections.habitat: Records associate it with rocky karst, including limestone forest, scrub and bamboo-covered slopes.
sections.diet: Its diet has not been described adequately in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: It is reported as nocturnal, but its movements and social behavior remain unknown.
sections.reproduction: The available species accounts provide no reliable details on breeding.
sections.ecology: Later surveys recorded it in Vietnam as well as Laos; one study then knew only a handful of sites across this limestone region.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database lists its IUCN status as Not Evaluated. Field researchers reported trapping and habitat disturbance at known Vietnamese sites.
